key_insight: Turbulence in a T-shaped mixer develops in two stages: a near-junction jet-like transitional regime followed by a decay region with power-law dissipation and scalar-variance decay before relaxing to duct flow.
engineering_relevance: These results clarify how turbulent mixing evolves in T-junction devices, helping engineers better predict mixing efficiency and design channel geometries for chemical processing.
method: Direct numerical simulations of the turbulent regime in a T-shaped mixer
Reynolds numbers up to Re = 2000 at Schmidt number Sc = 1
Streamwise analysis of velocity, turbulent kinetic energy, dissipation, and scalar variance
evidence_signal: The study reports distinct power-law exponents in the decay region, with velocity statistics matching bounded-domain decaying turbulence and scalar variance matching unbounded-turbulence behavior, supported by time-averaged scalar profiles and an effective diffusion coefficient.
watch_item: The apparent mismatch between velocity and scalar decay laws suggests that mixing progression across the channel cross-section may complicate model transfer to other geometries or higher Schmidt-number fluids.
paper_title: Stages of turbulence generation and decay in a T-shaped mixer
